chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Aban ibn Uthman, from whoever informed him, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'Why was the House (Kaaba) named al-Atiq (the Free)?' He said: 'It is a free house, freed from the people. No one has ever owned it.'

key_terms.الْبَيْتُ الْعَتِيقُ: Al-Bayt al-Atiq — the Free House, a Quranic name for the Kaaba meaning freed from human ownership
key_terms.حُرٌّ: Hurr — free, liberated; denotes freedom from human subjugation or ownership
key_terms.عَتِيقٌ: Atiq — freed, liberated; also carries the meaning of 'ancient' or 'noble' in Arabic

ai.seo_question: Why is the Kaaba called al-Bayt al-Atiq (the Free House) in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) explains the meaning behind the name 'al-Bayt al-Atiq' (the Free House), one of the Quran's names for the Kaaba (22:29, 22:33). The Imam teaches that the Kaaba's freedom (hurriya/itq) means it belongs to no person or sovereign — it is God's house alone, beyond human ownership or possession. This understanding would have been significant in the early Islamic world where sanctuary sites were sometimes claimed by tribal or political authorities.
